notes.title: Narrative Alchemy: Words Craft Worlds
notes.notes: [p][/p][p]Hey everyone, I thought I’d give you an inside view into what the Narrative Department does at Nesting.  [/p][p]There’s not a lot of knowledge of what we do – a lot of people outside games think we’re simply “writers”, but it’s a lot more complicated than that. [/p][p]Sure, we write the game – but we design the players’ experience through the environment, lore, characters, interactions, and more. This means we write the cutscenes, the voice over you never think about (like the character grunts after being shot, running and out of breath, etc.), and also construct the bios of all of the characters and NPCs, name everyone, give them voices by writing their dialogue and reference notes for the voice actors and voice over director, write screenplay notes for the actors for cutscenes (it also helps the Animation and Art department, directors, and so on).  [/p][p]We track all player choices, but also tie everything together – sort of like knitting a sweater out of a ball of yarn. We move around in time but have to keep the relationships and plot in mind, writing some content in the end game, but then revising mid-game content, before reviewing scripts for the beginning quests. [/p][p]Revisions are essential. We revise and edit a LOT of content as the game develops, it’s never a situation where we write something and leave it alone. Remember writing in school and having to revise your papers? It’s that, over and over and over again. For some, that might be torture – but for others, you polish something with every editorial pass. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45469487/4d2aaa72a11191089a87eda34a519a5c5b78a7e6.png"][/img][/p][p]We also test out our content – playing the game and making sure the experience “hits” the way it should, that the moments are felt by the team (and hopefully later by you, the players!).  [/p][p]When we go to record voice overs or performance capture for cinematics, Narrative is on hand as a full resource for the actors and directors – giving context to make the performances their best. It’s so important because with a branching storyline, the scripts can get incredibly confusing on paper (and digitally)! Subtle nuance in performance is essential to making your unique playthrough feel different than another. [/p][p]I love what I do. In Narrative, we pitch new ideas like quest lines, lore, and write the in-game texts and codex to unify the team’s creative vision. There’s always something more to do, another story breadcrumb, another line of dialogue.  [/p][p]I love it! It’s really fun, but sometimes there’s also drudgery: [/p][p][i]Spreadsheets.[/i] [/p][p]I’d rather be forced to attend a thousand meetings that could have been an email than work in spreadsheets – but they’re a known evil.  [/p][p]We need to organize data – from tracking relationships to dialogue choices, plot points, and more. [/p][p]So, I balance a lot of different tasks (with the occasional spreadsheet) to build the world, the characters, and everything in between! Tadaah! [/p][p]-Miranda [/p]

notes.title: Dressing the World: NPC Design in Progress
notes.notes: [p]Hey everyone,[/p][p][/p][p]It’s been a while. We’ve been quiet because we’ve been hard at work building a demo we think you’ll enjoy.[/p][p][/p][p]In the meantime, here’s a look at what we’re doing with NPC characters. These shots show clothing for our generic male models. Female characters aren’t ready yet, and we’ve only added one face so far, so yes, everyone’s a clone for now. That’ll change soon.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45469487/e6f41bfe0d79c2a79b29fe22382962e5003c8caa.jpg"][/img][/p][p]We’ve put a lot of work into systems that make clothes easy to customize, like changing patterns, colors, and logos. Since LA is packed with unique brands and sports teams, we need more than just color swaps to capture that variety.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45469487/3a727e1ffe8cf8406fe2ef7bcadf9c0f90b9f46f.jpg"][/img][/p][p]We’ve also built tools to change hair color and add tattoos to limbs and torsos. Tattoos are key to gang identity, so they’ll help show which faction someone belongs to.[/p][p][/p][p]All this visual detail helps ground the world in reality. That way, when missions take you into the surreal parts filled with rust, monsters, and smog, the contrast hits harder.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45469487/262a30594e4760f5f0268cde3429ac5da8171d5a.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Since we’re a small team, we’ve focused on making character creation fast. One big time-saver is our modular atlas. It’s a library of zippers, buttons, chains, and more. Each piece can be colored directly in Unreal. Need a brass chain and a green clip? No problem. No new textures needed.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45469487/7e86d6a73d58df84d303726add7075ca6e6e761c.jpg"][/img][/p][p]More soon![/p]

notes.title: Dev Diary: Custom Weapons and Other Weird Experiments
notes.notes:
Hi All, Seb here with another dev diary!

We’ve been deep in production, getting the game ready for our upcoming early access launch. No, we haven’t locked in a date yet, but it’s coming soon! 

One of the perks of being a tiny (micro?) team is that we can move fast and add cool stuff whenever the game feels like it needs it. No endless meetings or having to defend every decision. We just build what feels right, and that freedom to improvise makes a big difference.
And honestly, doing this independently means we get to be as weird as we want, and that’s my favorite part. I’ve always admired those early 8-bit devs who made games without anybody telling them what to do. Or maybe I’m romanticizing it?

One of my friends summed it up best when I told them about this project: “Go big and go weird.” (Hi K!) Luckily, that’s exactly what we’re doing here at Nesting. In the upcoming months we’ll be showing you more weirdly cool stuff about the game. We’ve barely scratched the surface.
But today, I want to share something one of our talented team members came up with: customizable weapons! Totally unplanned, but the moment he showed us his mockups, we were all excited. 

It’s fun, and it adds something special, don’t you think?

notes.title: Dev Diary: Who is Kana Luna aka Mercury?
notes.notes:
Who is Kana Luna aka Mercury?
Kana was a student at UCLA, trying to figure out what she wanted to do with her life. She studied criminology…
She was supposed to be a cop, just like her mom. Following in her footsteps wasn’t as easy as she thought. While in school, Kana struggled with visions, leading her to drop out.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45469487/1362fbb78d5a2077d0f88c6ef128db895a0584da.png[/img]

Her student loans? They didn’t wait, and she found herself with a bill she couldn’t possibly afford. She learned about a job that paid well, really well. Kana met Callisto (the guy from the trailer) and started delivering packages for the Costa Muerta, the local Syndicate.
Before she knew it, Kana witnessed a murder and went on the run. Callisto trained her to fight back, to be deadly, to become an Enforcer. As Mercury, she hunted the man chasing her and unlocked her latent magical powers.
Now, Mercury has returned to Los Angeles for work. She’s caught up in a supernatural war between Syndicates and investigating a magical serial killer using her visions of the past to guide her, her gun to protect her, and her magic to flatten enemies into paste.
“So much for a warm welcome…”
She’s not sure who she is, or who she’s supposed to become – but her story is in your hands…
Coming soon…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45469487/8e0ff1c7edfbb142d45f7da9b9e0b80327a91cb1.png[/img]

Just so you know, that’s my absolute favorite outfit! :)

Miranda!
(your friendly narrative designer)

notes.title: Dev Diary: Bringing Directorate Novitiate to Handheld!
notes.notes:
Great news! We ran our first tests on Directorate Novitiate running on the Steam Deck yesterday, and the results were amazing! The game runs smoothly, the visuals hold up beautifully, and the controls feel right at home on the handheld.

Our team did an amazing job optimizing the game during development, and that effort is really paying off. Thanks to their hard work, bringing it to handheld feels totally possible!

Of course, we’ve still got some optimization and fine-tuning ahead: tweaking performance, adjusting UI scaling, and making sure everything feels just right. But even at this stage, it's already shaping up to be a fantastic experience. 

How important is playing on devices like the Steam Deck to you?

Seb

notes.title: Dev News: What We’ve Been Up To This Week!
notes.notes:
It’s been another busy week at Nesting Games as we keep working hard on the game, and we’ve got some updates to share!

Miranda Pellegrino, our fearless narrative designer, sat down with Gaming.net for an [url=https://www.gaming.net/miranda-pellegrino-lead-narrative-designer-for-nesting-games-talks-the-directorate-novitiate-interview-series/]interview[/url] to share new details about the story.

We also traveled to Toronto for the Canadian Game Awards, where we [url=https://youtu.be/lZB_FbzriPY?si=RX0HV4Bsdt6HWwGD]showcased our preview trailer[/url]. As developers, we rarely get to see audience reactions in real time, so experiencing that firsthand was incredibly satisfying. 

Thursdays at Nesting are all about playing the game. The team gets together, both in the studio and online, to test the latest version, eat too many snacks, take notes, and brainstorm improvements. It’s my favorite part of game development, and it works especially well with a small team. Everyone gets a say, a chance to contribute, and a role in shaping the game. And it just makes the whole process more fun!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45469487/86b517300685cc54800fff625bbc81fe0b20f52e.png[/img]

In the coming weeks, we’ll share more details beyond the preview trailer—especially about our main character, Mercury (aka Kana Luna). Who is she? Where does she come from? And why does she wear sunglasses at night?

If there’s something you’d like to know, jump into the discussion section and chat with the dev team. We’d love to hear from you !

Seb

notes.title: Making Enemies (In a Good Way): Félix’s Dev Diary
notes.notes:
Hi everyone, Félix here! I’m the youngest at Nesting and I’m the primary gameplay programmer. This is my first game fresh out of university. Programming is the best way I have found to get closer to the games I love. I’ve been playing games since I was little. My goal is to at least try every genre of games at least once.
 
My role at Nesting is to work on anything enemy related. (Except character art!!! You don’t want me to do art, trust me!!!) I am also the in-house reference when it comes to combat mechanics and how they are integrated.
My favorite part about working on the game has been working on unique enemies and bosses. They have so much potential, and you don’t feel restricted working on them. You can be as extravagant as you want and break gameplay conventions. They are also a great way to combine gameplay and storytelling in a climactic way for the player.
 
Speaking of… I am currently working on a unique enemy that will show up early in the game. I hope you love him as much as we do.
 
Sneak peek time!!

notes.title: Dev Diary: Meet the Narrative Designer!
notes.notes:
Hi, everyone! I’m Miranda, your friendly American transplant and Lead Narrative Designer in snowy Quebec City! I’m in charge of writing the codex, dialogue, cinematics, quests, storyline, and so on.
Lately, I’ve been working on quests for other regions of the game. I’m also updating content in-game, like quest objectives and codex entries for characters, item descriptions, locations, equipment, etc. Oh, and casting! It’s been especially fun writing scripts for voice actor auditions.
Basically, I write a lot – from notes, to powerpoint presentations, to emails, to spreadsheets, to scripts – and then I have to edit it down like crazy. Then my amazing coworkers turn my writing into magic! Once they’ve integrated everything into the game, I play the quests, testing them and seeing if the storylines really hit home or need further revising. It’s an incredible collaboration process!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45469487/d0b0d825724f46b61fd69bf6003c557cfd316e4c.jpg[/img]
 
Anyway, here’s a sneak peek at some of the content I’m working on!

Codex Entry : Draft
Kana Luna / Mercury
Age: 24
Kana Luna is a former college drop-out that turned to working for a cartel to pay her debts. After witnessing a murder, Kana fled to Mexico with her boss and mentor, Callisto. She trained there for two years and became Mercury, an agent of the Costa Muerta. The Luna family has no idea what Kana’s been up to and neither does her best friend, Mort. She has a younger brother named Akio. Her parents are Alejandro and Yua Luna.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45469487/e5fe07ff022bdac58bc8744a0fd6a57615de5268.gif[/img]

Because we’re a small studio, we have to play a lot of different roles. Your feedback is important to us and helps us make a better game. Please think of yourself as part of the team!
I’m so excited to have you here with us and I cannot wait for you the play the game.

-Miranda

PS: What are everyday things Kana (or you) can’t live without?

notes.title: Welcome to The Directorate: Novitiate!
notes.notes:
Hey everyone,
We’re thrilled to finally share what we’ve been working on. The Directorate: Novitiate is a third-person action RPG that blends gunplay, magic, and impactful choices into one immersive experience. We couldn’t be more excited to introduce you to the world we’ve created.

Set in 2006 Los Angeles, you step into the role of Kana Luna—codename Mercury. Returning to a city filled with secrets, you find yourself drawn into the Directorate, a powerful and dangerous underground criminal organization. As a novitiate, you’ll rise through the ranks, mastering firearms, magic, and acrobatic combat while navigating a web of intrigue and danger.

Beyond the action, the story offers deep narrative choices. A supernatural serial killer is on the loose, and every decision you make will shape your journey. Who do you trust? Do you remain loyal to the Directorate, or fight to retain your humanity? The choices are yours, and they matter.

We’ve got a lot more to share soon, including gameplay mechanics, story insights, and ways for you to get involved. For now, we just wanted to say hello, introduce the game, and let you know that we’re listening. Have questions Anything you'd like to see? Drop them in the comments, we’d love to hear from you.

Stay tuned, this is just the beginning!
